title: 1 Oct 2026 (Cairo)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Cairo test centre, 1 October 2026

questions.question: A toddler develops ataxia a few days after a URTI; CT brain is normal. What is the diagnosis?
Which condition causes a false negative Mantoux test?
Which condition causes a false negative sweat chloride test?
Which element is essential for valid informed consent?
questions.exp: Valid consent needs capacity, information, understanding and voluntariness.
questions.d: The patient understands the information and agrees voluntarily

questions.question: Where should a new children's hospital be built?
questions.a: In an area with a large number of children

questions.question: Which strategy most reliably improves patient safety?
questions.exp: Forcing functions (for example incompatible connectors) are the strongest system fixes.
questions.b: Forcing functions that make errors impossible

questions.question: A mother still refuses vaccination after counselling. What should be done?
questions.exp: Saudi law makes core vaccines mandatory. The recall writer chose reporting to the authority.
questions.c: Document and follow local policy, which may require informing the authority

questions.question: Which principle justifies public health measures that limit individual choice?
Which ethical theory judges actions by their purpose or outcome?
questions.exp: Teleological ethics judges acts by consequences; deontology by duty.

questions.question: A colleague doctor is addicted to drugs. What should you do first?
questions.exp: Patient safety may require reporting if he continues to practise.
questions.b: Talk to him privately and advise him to seek help (escalate if patients are at risk)

questions.question: A doctor connected an oxygen line to an IV cannula, harming the patient. What type of failure is this?
questions.exp: Active failures are unsafe acts by front-line staff; latent conditions are system weaknesses.

questions.question: An error in a neonate with HIE was caught before reaching the baby. What is this?
A 2-week-old has abdominal distension and milky vomiting; rectal examination shows an empty rectum with good tone followed by a gush of meconium. What is the diagnosis?
After Hirschsprung pull-through a baby has abdominal pain and distension. Besides broad-spectrum antibiotics, what is the treatment?
A child has retching, vomiting and abdominal pain, and contrast shows obstruction at the pylorus. What is the management?
questions.exp: Gastric volvulus or obstruction needs surgery.

questions.question: A 4-year-old girl has bloody diarrhoea, perianal skin tags and inflamed mucosa on endoscopy. What is the diagnosis?
An infant with a large VSD has pulmonary hypertension and heart failure despite medical treatment. What is next?
A child with tetralogy of Fallot has a hypercyanotic spell with tachycardia and low BP that does not settle with knee-chest position, oxygen and morphine. What is given to raise systemic resistance?
questions.exp: Phenylephrine raises SVR; IV propranolol or esmolol relaxes the infundibulum. With hypotension, phenylephrine is preferred. The recall writer chose propranolol.

questions.question: An infant has vomiting from day 1 that worsens over 3 days, mild dehydration, slightly low sodium and high creatinine. What is the next investigation?
questions.exp: Early progressive vomiting can be metabolic; also exclude obstruction with contrast. The recall writer was unsure.

questions.question: A child has fever then rash with posterior auricular and suboccipital lymph nodes. What is the diagnosis?
An unvaccinated 3-year-old has a typical rash after cough and coryza, and a neighbour had the same. What is the diagnosis?
A child has fever for 4-5 days, conjunctival injection and a rash prominent in the groin. What is the treatment?
A baby has tachypnoea and HR 300/min. What is the next investigation?
After a drug ingestion a child has HR 200 with SVT on ECG and is stable. What is the treatment?
A child swallowed his grandmother's tricyclic antidepressant pills. What is a poor prognostic sign?
An infant has hepatomegaly, raised liver enzymes and hypoglycaemia. Which test confirms tyrosinaemia type 1?
What is an absolute contraindication to breastfeeding?
questions.exp: Also maternal HIV (in high-income settings), HTLV and some drugs.

questions.question: A baby of an HBsAg-positive mother had vaccine and HBIG within 12 hours. What is the advice on breastfeeding?
An infant has bilious vomiting. The junior orders a test; the senior says it is not needed. What is the right test?
questions.exp: Bilious vomiting needs urgent exclusion of malrotation.

questions.question: A 9-year-old with oesophageal varices is bleeding, with Hb 9.1, HR 170 and unstable BP. What is the first step?
questions.exp: Stabilise first, then octreotide and endoscopy.
questions.b: Oxygen and IV fluid resuscitation (then blood)

questions.question: When entering the room of a patient on contact precautions, what is put on first?
questions.exp: Donning order: gown, mask, goggles, gloves.

questions.question: How do you protect yourself from droplet infection?
A child coming for vaccines has a household member on chemotherapy. Which vaccine should not be given?
An asthmatic child had a PICU admission with cyanosis. What long-term treatment is needed?
A newborn has respiratory distress after contact with a grandmother with a respiratory infection. What is the likely cause?
A 2-week-old has frequent nasal blockage with clear discharge but feeds well and is thriving. What is the management?
questions.exp: Neonates are obligate nasal breathers; saline drops help.

questions.question: A baby has cyanosis when feeding that improves on crying, ear anomalies, a heart murmur and genital anomalies. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Coloboma, Heart, Atresia choanae, Retardation, Genital, Ear anomalies (CHD7).

questions.question: A 6-week-old has respiratory distress, cyanosis and cardiomegaly with heart failure. What is given?
questions.exp: At 6 weeks the duct is closed; heart failure from cardiomyopathy or myocarditis needs inodilators.

questions.question: A child with ALL on chemotherapy has high fever and looks unwell with no focus. What is the empirical treatment?
An immunocompromised child was exposed to a sibling with chickenpox a few hours ago. What should be given?
Several schoolchildren develop jaundice and high liver enzymes after eating the same food. What is the test?
A child with otitis media is improving on treatment, but the eardrum is still mildly red. Is he due vaccines today?
questions.exp: Mild illness is not a contraindication to vaccination.
questions.a: Delay until the drum is normal

questions.question: An infant with RSV bronchiolitis improves, then suddenly worsens with lethargy and fever. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Late deterioration suggests a bacterial complication.
questions.c: Secondary bacterial infection (bacteraemia or otitis media)

questions.question: A 3-year-old with recurrent wheeze has an acute attack with bilateral wheeze. What is the first treatment?
A child has wide fixed splitting of S2. What is the diagnosis?
After a car accident a 9-year-old is intubated with a rigid distended abdomen and femur fracture and has had 60 mL/kg saline; HR 105, BP 91/50. What is next?
Which test supports a diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome?
What is the treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome with loss of walking?
A child admitted for dehydration develops leg weakness, areflexia and loss of bladder control. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Bladder involvement points to the cord.

questions.question: A child with a facial port-wine stain and seizures has leptomeningeal angioma. Which complication should be looked for?
An infant has developmental regression and clusters of spasms with hypsarrhythmia. What is the diagnosis?
A child has seizures, facial angiofibromas, hypopigmented macules and learning problems. What is the diagnosis?
Which genetic condition is associated with optic pathway glioma?
An 18-month-old has low weight-for-height with normal height-for-age. What is this?
questions.exp: Wasting reflects acute malnutrition; stunting chronic.

questions.question: A boy's parents are 180 cm and 160 cm. What is his target height range?
An infant has a high-pitched cat-like cry and microcephaly. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: 5p- syndrome; the recall item had no answer.

questions.question: A neonate has cleft lip and palate and hypoglycaemia. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Midline defects with GH and ACTH deficiency.

questions.question: What is it called when a person has two different mutant alleles at the same locus?
questions.exp: The recall item had no answer.

questions.question: A boy has features of fragile X syndrome. What is the investigation?
An infant has hypotonia and tongue fasciculations. What is the investigation?
A child has features of dermatomyositis. What is the first test?
What is a severe digital complication of scleroderma?
A child has recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhoea and skin lesions. What is the first investigation?
questions.exp: Antibody deficiency causes sinopulmonary and GI infection.

questions.question: An asthmatic child has sudden respiratory distress, hyper-resonance and reduced air entry on one side. What is the first step?
A child with CVID has chronic diarrhoea and recurrent chest infections. Which organism commonly causes the diarrhoea?
questions.exp: Giardia is classic in antibody deficiency; Cryptosporidium in T-cell defects. Recall options were Cryptosporidium, Aspergillus and TB.

questions.question: A 3-year-old has meningitis with seizures and an unclear Gram stain. What is the empirical treatment?
A 2-month-old has Hb 9.1, MCV 85 and retics 2%, with normal platelets. What is the management?
A 2-month-old has severe pallor, Hb 4 g/dL and reticulocytes 0.1%, with normal WBC and platelets. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pure red cell aplasia in infancy, often with thumb anomalies and macrocytosis.

questions.question: A child has microcytic hypochromic anaemia and koilonychia. What is the best confirmatory test?
A boy has leg bone pain, high ALP, low calcium and high creatinine. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: High creatinine points to CKD-mineral bone disease. The recall writer chose nutritional rickets.

questions.question: An infant's head grew from 35 to 47 cm with normal feeding. What is the imaging?
A NICU infant with a UVC develops haematuria. What is the investigation?
A boy has UTI symptoms, pyuria, microscopic haematuria and high-normal BP. Which renal imaging assesses scarring?
questions.exp: DMSA. Culture is still needed for diagnosis.

questions.question: Which condition contraindicates intraosseous access in a bone?
questions.exp: Also osteogenesis imperfecta, fracture or infection at the site.

questions.question: A baby has a congenital nasal mass. What imaging excludes intracranial extension?
What is the most common type of choanal atresia?
After surgery for transposition, an ECG shows sinus node dysfunction. What is it?
questions.exp: After atrial switch. Junctional ectopic tachycardia occurs early after surgery.

questions.question: A child has bruises of different ages and the mother says she will hurt him again. What should be done?
questions.b: Report to social services and protect the child

questions.question: A child with otitis media on antibiotics becomes increasingly irritable. What is next?
A diabetic child has white pseudomembranes on the buccal mucosa. What is the diagnosis?
A girl has fruity breath, hyperglycaemia and metabolic acidosis. What is given first?
questions.exp: Fluids first, insulin infusion 1-2 hours later.

questions.question: A child has recurrent vomiting, bicarbonate 35, low sodium, chloride and magnesium. What urine test helps?
questions.exp: Low urine chloride means vomiting; high urine chloride suggests Bartter or Gitelman.

questions.question: At what age does separation anxiety usually begin?
questions.exp: Stranger and separation anxiety appear around 8-9 months and peak at 12-18 months.

questions.question: A child has poor social communication and restricted repetitive behaviours. What is the diagnosis?
A boy always argues with his father and blames others. What is the diagnosis?
A brother and sister fight, each believing the mother loves the other more. What should be done?
A child with recurrent chest problems has a normal examination except for a protruding sternum. What is the finding?
questions.exp: Can follow chronic airway disease; the recall was vague.

questions.question: A chest X-ray shows hyperinflation with cystic lesions throughout the right lung. What is next?
questions.exp: CT defines CPAM or lobar emphysema.

questions.question: A child has recurrent lower lobe infections and a lesion with systemic arterial supply. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn has developmental dysplasia of the hip. What is the treatment?
How is N-acetylcysteine given for paracetamol overdose?
questions.exp: Oral and IV NAC are equally effective; IV is preferred with vomiting. The recall writer chose oral better than IV.
questions.b: IV or oral are both effective

questions.question: A febrile child has been convulsing for 14 minutes. What is given?
A baby has lytic bone lesions, skin desquamation and snuffles. What is the diagnosis?
A girl has short stature and a webbed neck. What test confirms the diagnosis?
Which malignancy is increased in Down syndrome?
A boy has hyperactivity, school decline and skin hyperpigmentation. What is the investigation?
Which screening test supports ataxia telangiectasia?
A boy has small platelets, eczema and recurrent infections. What is the diagnosis?
A haemophilia patient's PTT does not correct after factor VIII doses. What is next?
A girl with normal development except speech delay has a family history of late talking. What is the first test?
A baby has hypotonia, prolonged jaundice and constipation. What is the diagnosis?
Which screening test confirms congenital hypothyroidism?
A child has an appendiceal abscess. What is the management?
questions.a: IV antibiotics with percutaneous drainage under imaging

questions.question: A child has recurrent vague periumbilical pain with nausea. What is the diagnosis?
A child has recurrent bitemporal headaches. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bilateral migraine is common in children.

questions.question: Which high-risk medicine is fatal in concentrated form and must be stored and diluted carefully?
After a car accident a child has a seat-belt sign across the abdomen. What is the investigation?
A child has offensive unilateral nasal discharge. What is the management?
questions.d: ENT removal of a nasal foreign body

questions.question: A coin is seen in the oesophagus on X-ray. What is the management?
questions.exp: Oesophageal coins should be removed. The recall writer chose fluoroscopy with magnet.

questions.question: A newborn has copious secretions, a coiled NG tube and no gas in the abdomen. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Gasless abdomen means no distal fistula.

questions.question: A child's height is on the 5th-25th centile, the examination is normal and family members are tall. What is the management?
An infant is fussy and spits up after feeds but thrives. What is the diagnosis?
A child using nasal steroids has epistaxis. What is the common cause?
A baby with recurrent UTIs has grade 4 vesicoureteral reflux. What is the management?
questions.exp: Surgery for high-grade VUR with breakthrough infections. The recall writer chose ureteral reimplantation.
questions.a: Antibiotic prophylaxis; surgical reimplantation if breakthrough infections

questions.question: A child rescued from drowning has high blood glucose. What is the treatment?
questions.b: Supportive care with isotonic fluids; do not give insulin for stress hyperglycaemia

questions.question: A child has abdominal pain, joint pain and palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs. What is the diagnosis?
A neonate has melaena in the first days of life. Which test distinguishes swallowed maternal blood?
A contrast study shows bowel in the scrotum without strangulation. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Repair soon, as incarceration risk is high in infants.

questions.question: An infant has a scrotal swelling that transilluminates. What is the management?
A child on laxatives still has constipation. What is next?
A previously healthy adolescent who injects drugs has infective endocarditis. What is the most likely organism?
questions.exp: IV drug use: Staph aureus, often right-sided. The recall writer chose haemolytic streptococcus.

questions.question: Which cyanotic heart disease has decreased pulmonary blood flow?
After treatment for acute otitis media a child has middle ear effusion. What is next?
questions.exp: Most resolve within 3 months. The recall writer chose 2 months.

questions.question: A mother and child both have haematuria and the child has hearing loss. Which gene is affected?
What is the definitive treatment of congenital (Finnish) nephrotic syndrome?
Parents of a child with atypical HUS refuse life-saving dialysis. What should be done?
questions.exp: Life-saving treatment can proceed against parental refusal.
questions.a: Give dialysis in the child's best interest

questions.question: A post-pubertal girl with primary amenorrhoea has monthly lower abdominal pain and a lower abdominal mass. What is the investigation?
An asthmatic child has daily symptoms and FEV1 60-80%. How is it classified?
questions.exp: Daily symptoms and FEV1 60-80% is moderate persistent (NAEPP). The recall said FEV1 < 70%.

questions.question: A child is HBsAg positive, anti-HBc total positive and anti-HBc IgM negative. What is the status?
Which complication may occur two weeks into bacterial meningitis?
questions.exp: Subdural effusion is common (Hib, pneumococcus). The recall writer chose epidural haemorrhage.

questions.question: A child with adenoid hypertrophy has disturbed sleep. What is the investigation?
A child in cardiac arrest has organised electrical activity but no pulse. What is this?
questions.exp: CPR and adrenaline; treat reversible causes.

questions.question: A child has focal seizures with eye blinking and no cranial nerve signs. What is the investigation?
What is a common complication of tetralogy of Fallot?
A child has eye blinking tics that progressed to vocal tics. How is it diagnosed?
A child has tingling in the legs and peaked T waves on ECG. What is given?
A child develops flushing (red man syndrome) during a 1-hour vancomycin infusion. What should be done?
questions.exp: Red man syndrome is infusion-rate related; report through pharmacovigilance (SFDA in Saudi Arabia).
questions.d: Stop or slow the infusion, give an antihistamine, and report the adverse drug reaction

questions.question: A child stung by a scorpion has systemic symptoms. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Antivenom for systemic envenomation, prazosin for hypertension.

questions.question: A neonate has seizures with blood glucose 20 mg/dL. What is the treatment?
questions.d: 2 mL/kg 10% dextrose bolus then infusion at 6-8 mg/kg/min

questions.question: A young child has rhythmic thigh rubbing with flushing, alert and stoppable. What is the management?
